The fitted spline smoothers remain close to the horizontal line at the nominal median of 0.50 across the operational range of each predictor. This confirms that the linear and logarithmic transformations adequately account for risk variation across interest rates, revolving credit lines, income levels, and inquiry counts without material functional-form distortion.

### C.2. Risk-Decile Calibration Breakdown and Grouped Dispersion Analysis
In Section 3.4, the grouped dispersion test across ten predicted risk deciles flagged elevated between-decile variation ($p = `r sprintf("%.4f", decile_dispersion$p.value)`$). Table 16 profiles conditional fitted-sample calibration and grouped DHARMa scaled residuals across each predicted-risk decile to identify the source of this signal.

```{r dharma_decile_investigation, echo=FALSE}
decile_diag <- ext_train |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    fitted_pd = sim_res$fittedPredictedResponse,
    risk_decile = risk_decile
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(risk_decile) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n = dplyr::n(),
    mean_predicted_pd = mean(fitted_pd),
    observed_default_rate = mean(repay_fail),
    calibration_difference = observed_default_rate - mean_predicted_pd,
    binomial_se = sqrt(mean_predicted_pd * (1 - mean_predicted_pd) / n),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dharma_scaled_res = decile_residuals$scaledResiduals)

decile_table_df <- data.frame(
  Decile = decile_diag$risk_decile,
  `Applications (N)` = format(decile_diag$n, big.mark = ","),
  `Mean Predicted PD` = sprintf("%.2f%%", decile_diag$mean_predicted_pd * 100),
  `Observed Default Rate` = sprintf("%.2f%%", decile_diag$observed_default_rate * 100),
  `Difference` = sprintf("%+.2f%%", decile_diag$calibration_difference * 100),
  `Binomial SE` = sprintf("%.4f", decile_diag$binomial_se),
  `Grouped Residual` = sprintf("%.4f", decile_diag$dharma_scaled_res),
  check.names = FALSE
)

kable(decile_table_df, booktabs = TRUE, caption = "Conditional fitted-sample calibration and grouped DHARMa residual breakdown") |>
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position", font_size = 7.8)
```

Inspection of Table 16 clarifies the empirical mechanism producing the grouped dispersion signal:

1. **Low-Risk Deciles (1–2):** The model slightly overpredicts default risk (Decile 1: predicted 3.72% vs. observed 3.16%, $\Delta = -0.57\%$; Decile 2: predicted 5.71% vs. observed 5.07%, $\Delta = -0.63\%$). Given the large sample size ($N \approx 3,074$ per decile), these slight negative calibration offsets shift aggregated scaled residuals toward the lower theoretical margin (0.0013 and 0.0084).
2. **Intermediate-to-High Risk Deciles (6–8):** The model modestly underpredicts default risk by 2.2 to 2.4 percentage points (Decile 6: predicted 12.83% vs. observed 15.06%, $\Delta = +2.23\%$; Decile 7: predicted 15.22% vs. observed 17.64%, $\Delta = +2.42\%$; Decile 8: predicted 18.41% vs. observed 20.66%, $\Delta = +2.25\%$). Relative to binomial standard errors ($\text{SE} \approx 0.0060$ to $0.0070$), these deviations correspond to approximately +3.2 to +3.7 standard errors, placing aggregated scaled residuals close to the upper theoretical margin (0.9872, 0.9875, and 0.9728).
3. **Highest-Risk Decile (10):** In the highest-risk decile, predicted default probability (34.89%) closely matches observed default frequency (34.88%, $\Delta = -0.00002$).

Evaluating residual stability across alternative binning resolutions confirms that uniformity is preserved under 5 quintiles ($D = 0.3145, p = 0.6068$), 10 deciles ($D = `r sprintf("%.4f", unname(decile_uniformity$statistic))`, p = `r sprintf("%.4f", decile_uniformity$p.value)`$), and 20 ventiles ($D = 0.1957, p = 0.3782$). The dispersion test statistic attenuates as resolution increases, showing significance under 5 groups ($\text{ratio} = 3.4593, p = 0.0120$) and 10 groups ($\text{ratio} = `r sprintf("%.4f", unname(decile_dispersion$statistic))`, p = `r sprintf("%.4f", decile_dispersion$p.value)`$), but becoming non-significant under 20 groups ($\text{ratio} = 1.5111, p = 0.1860$). This pattern demonstrates that the signal is driven by coarse group aggregation rather than systematic borrower-level distributional breakdown. Prudential governance requires tracking these intermediate-tier deciles across future out-of-sample vintages.

### C.3. Simulation Sensitivity and Outlier Stability
Table 17 evaluates diagnostic sensitivity across three simulation depths ($N_{\text{sim}} \in \{500, 1000, 2000\}$) generated under the conditional simulation configuration.

```{r dharma_sensitivity_table, echo=FALSE}
run_dharma_sensitivity <- function(n_simulations, seed = 42) {
  sim <- DHARMa::simulateResiduals(
    fittedModel = m4_st_glmm,
    n = n_simulations,
    seed = seed,
    refit = FALSE,
    simulateREs = "conditional"
  )
  out <- DHARMa::testOutliers(sim, plot = FALSE, type = "binomial")
  uniform <- DHARMa::testUniformity(sim, plot = FALSE)
  dispersion <- DHARMa::testDispersion(sim, plot = FALSE)
  n_observations <- length(sim$scaledResiduals)
  expected <- n_observations * 2 / (n_simulations + 1)
  data.frame(
    Simulations = n_simulations,
    Observed_outliers = as.integer(unname(out$statistic)),
    Expected_outliers = round(expected, 1),
    Outlier_p = out$p.value,
    Uniformity_p = uniform$p.value,
    Dispersion_ratio = as.numeric(unname(dispersion$statistic)),
    Dispersion_p = dispersion$p.value
  )
}

sens_table <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  run_dharma_sensitivity(500),
  run_dharma_sensitivity(1000),
  run_dharma_sensitivity(2000)
)

sens_display <- data.frame(
  `Simulations` = sens_table$Simulations,
  `Obs. Outliers` = sens_table$Observed_outliers,
  `Exp. Outliers` = sprintf("%.1f", sens_table$Expected_outliers),
  `Outlier p` = sprintf("%.4f", sens_table$Outlier_p),
  `Uniformity p` = sprintf("%.4f", sens_table$Uniformity_p),
  `Disp. Ratio` = sprintf("%.4f", sens_table$Dispersion_ratio),
  `Dispersion p` = sprintf("%.4f", sens_table$Dispersion_p),
  check.names = FALSE
)

kable(sens_display, booktabs = TRUE, align = "rcccccc", caption = "DHARMa diagnostic sensitivity across simulation depths") |>
  kable_styling(latex_options = c("hold_position", "scale_down"), font_size = 8)
```

Across all tested simulation depths in Table 17, the outlier test, uniformity test, and dispersion test show consistent stability with no statistically significant departures from theoretical distributions ($p > 0.05$).

The conditional simulation identified `r observed_outliers` boundary observations compared with `r sprintf("%.1f", expected_outliers)` expected under 1,000 simulations ($p = `r sprintf("%.4f", outlier_test$p.value)`$). Standardized mean differences between outlier accounts and conforming accounts remain small across all key financial indicators ($|\text{SMD}| < 0.25$: annual income $\text{SMD} = -0.019$, revolving utilization $\text{SMD} = 0.042$, credit inquiries $\text{SMD} = 0.081$, interest rate $\text{SMD} = 0.088$, and revolving balance $\text{SMD} = -0.012$). These small differences indicate no evidence of data corruption or recording errors.

Re-simulating from the fitted random effects distribution (`simulateREs = "user-specified"`, `re.form = NA`, $N = 1,000$) confirmed acceptable uniformity ($D = 0.0065, p = 0.144$) and dispersion ($\text{ratio} = 1.0415, p = 0.204$), supporting hierarchical model adequacy.
